messages:
maria: kicking off AKS bring-up in eu-central2 for customer X. created cluster + GPU nodepool but seeing pod egress failures to our on-prem SD-WAN. filing here in case someone else hit this.

sam: ok — what's failing exactly? curl timeouts, DNS, or connectivity drops?

maria: curl to internal services over the tunnel times out. outside-in looks fine. `kubectl get pods` shows Ready but app logs show upstream connection errors.

lee: can you paste `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `ip a` from one of the gpu nodes? curious about MTU. AKS defaults sometimes keep 1500 and our SD-WAN wants 1400.

maria: grabbing now.

maria: ```
NAME                               STATUS   ROLES   AGE   VERSION     INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION
aks-eu-1-0                         Ready    agent   12m   v1.27.6     10.240.0.5     <none>        Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS     5.15.0-1023-aufs
```

maria: node `eth0` MTU shows 1500.

anita: yep that matches. the SD-WAN overlay is 1400, we saw packet fragmentation and TCP stalls at scale when MTU mismatches. AKS uses Azure CNI; need to tune the VNet subnet MTU or enable Azure CNI custom MTU if available.

jordan-oncall: quick mitigation: set `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on nodes and add iptables rule to MSS clamp on the node egress to tunnel IPs. Not ideal but fast.

sam: is this specific to GPU nodepool (NVIDIA drivers) or cluster-wide?

maria: both — same behavior from cpu nodes too. but GPU pods are more chatty and hit it faster. also saw occasional `nvidia` driver log noise during boot: `modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/...` — might be unrelated but worried about node image mismatch.

lee: for driver noise, check the aks GPU node image version. We should have `azure-ml-nvidia` preinstalled on our curated images. Which VM SKU are you using?

maria: Standard_NC6s_v3 for the pool. Image `aks-ubuntu-2204-azuregpu-2025-01-10`

platform-ops: flagging CIAM quota check — eu-central2 has reduced NC-series quota for our subscription. Did you hit any pending allocations?

maria: yes, one provisioning attempt failed with `AllocationFailed: not enough capacity`. I retried with spot fallback then used reserved. put that in the runbook notes.

anita: proposed plan: 1) Add MTU clamp mss rule on node startup via a node-init systemd unit (short-term). 2) Update vnet/subnet MTU or request Azure to enable custom MTU on CNI (longer-term). 3) Validate GPU node image matches our curated release and rebuild nodepool if driver missing. 4) Document quota/reservation steps to avoid AllocationFailed.

maria: implementing mss clamp now. adding a small systemd unit under `/etc/systemd/system/mtu-clamp.service` with: ```
[Unit]
Description=Clamp MSS for SD-WAN
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/sbin/iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
ExecStart=/sbin/sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

devops-bot: deploy job queued: `nodepool/mtu-clamp` -> 3 nodes, rolling.

sam: after clamp, test with `curl --interface <pod-ip> http://internal-service:8080/health` and `iperf` between pod and onprem to confirm no fragmentation.

maria: patch rolled out to 3 nodes. initial curl looks better, tcp retransmits dropped significantly. still going to coordinate with Azure to see if we can change Azure CNI MTU or move to flannel with lower MTU for this cluster.

anita: for handoff: update the cluster bootstrap playbook to include: explicit MTU validation (compare node `ip link` MTU vs expected tunnel MTU), node image hash check (`/etc/os-release` + `uname -r` + `nvidia-smi` smoke), and quota/reservation checklist for NC-series in eu-central2.

maria: putting a short runbook snippet in the ticket and tagging infra-oncall. I'll create follow-up task to recreate the gpu nodepool with our curated image if driver issues persist.

jordan-oncall: thanks — marking as incident mitigated for now. add `:lock:` on the runbook section and handoff to platform-ops for the long-term fix.

platform-ops: acknowledged, will pick up Azure CNI escalation and quota planning. leaving notes in the cluster repo under `docs/bootstrap/aks-eu-central2.md`.

maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
